text:
selene: Quick sync after RFC review: we need a clear default egress behavior for Private customers. Two options we keep hearing: 1) default-to-shared-regional-relay and opt-in dedicated pools for enterprises, or 2) default-to-per-tenant-silos with opt-out to shared. Need to finalize so sales/infra teams have a single line to customers.

lian: +1 for default shared. Most customers don't need strict src-ip preservation and shared simplifies capacity planning. We should codify what "opt-in" looks like (SLA, pricing, lead time).

minh: compliance edge case: some customers require complete egress isolation (IP blocks dedicated, no shared hosts). Those must be accommodated via Dedicated. But for self-serve customers shared should be default.

amos: ops view: shared-relay reduces IP churn and NAT gateway counts. Also simplifies our metrics and autoscaler because we aggregate heat. Downsides: we must guarantee tenant tagging can't be spoofed and we need stronger telemetry per-tenant for billing/forensics.

jordyn: security/identity tradeoff: with shared relays we need a clear provenance header or mTLS client cert per tenant at the relay origin. Otherwise investigating cross-tenant incidents is painful. I prefer short-lived client certs issued from control plane per connection.

networking_bot: Note: rfc/2026 has hybrid recommendation in draft. CI: rfc/2026/tests 317 passed.

selene: operational concern: migration path for existing tenants on siloed pools -> shared pool (cost saving). We need a cutover plan that preserves customer IPs until cutover or provides an opt-in to release legacy IP blocks. Cutting IPs early breaks firewall allowlists.

lian: propose two migration modes:
```text
1) ip-preserve cutover: temporarily run dual-path (legacy egress still advertised) while we move flows, then announce IP retirement 30 days.
2) ip-rotate cutover: we provide new egress IPs and a helper agent to update allowlists via API for customers that allow automation.
```

minh: audit note: we must log and make accessible a "egress identity timeline" mapping session -> relay -> tenant to satisfy audit requests. That ties into jordyn's provenance header idea.

amos: cost modeling: shared default lowers committed capacity by ~18% in our Monte Carlo with 200 tenants. But if we allow unbounded tenant burst, tail provisioning still blows up. We need per-tenant burst quotas enforced at scheduler to give p99 stability.

jordyn: for enforcement we can do token-bucket per-tenant attached to the relay scheduler; this prevents noisy neighbors while retaining shared IPs. Also recommend connection-level labels so outbound providers can attribute.

selene: finalize feature list for RFC change: 1) default shared regional relay 2) dedicated pools as paid opt-in with lead time and IP reservation 3) migration modes (ip-preserve and ip-rotate) 4) per-tenant burst quotas + scheduler enforcement 5) provenance headers + short-lived client certs 6) audit timeline export API.

lian: I'll draft the opt-in sales playbook (pricing tiers, SLAs, lead time).

amos: I'll add quota enforcement hooks to the relay scheduler spike and simulate p99 under mixed workload by Thursday.

jordyn: I'll prototype cert issuance flow + provenance header schema and measure added latency on a small relay cluster.

minh: I'll pull two compliance customers and run the migration modes against their firewall rules to check practical blockers.

selene: One open question for architecture team: should relay-to-backend connections terminate TLS at relay (SNI routing) or do end-to-end TLS with pass-through? Passing TLS reduces ability to inject provenance headers but simplifies cert management for customers. Thoughts?

jordyn: prefer TLS termination at relay for the provenance header, but we must provide an opt-out E2E pass-through mode for customers that require cert pinning. That will be part of Dedicated pool feature set.

lian: sales-friendly phrasing: "Default fast path: shared regional egress (no per-tenant IPs). Upgrade to Dedicated egress for guaranteed IPs and SLAs." 

selene: ok, I'll update RFC and the infra tickets with the feature list and owners. Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the scheduler spike and cert latency numbers land. :white_check_mark:
